\label{lesson:BN-C50-dhoya}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for to put, then the Bengali for to open.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{ধোয়া}}
\textbf{\bn{ধোয়া}} — \emph{dhoyā} — \textquotedblleft{}to wash\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{ধোয়া}} (\emph{dhoyā}) is a tadbhava, a word inherited and reshaped by sound change. It comes from \emph{*dhauvati}, \textquotedblleft{}washes\textquotedblright{}, a form CDIAL reconstructs from its descendants (CDIAL 6886).
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{হাসা} (hāsā)}{হাসা (hāsā)}]{\bn{হাসা} (hāsā) — to laugh}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{হাসা}}
\textbf{\bn{হাসা}} — \emph{hāsā} — \textquotedblleft{}to laugh\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{হাসা}} (\emph{hāsā}) is a tadbhava, a word inherited and reshaped by sound change. It comes from \emph{*hasyate}, \textquotedblleft{}one laughs\textquotedblright{}, a form CDIAL reconstructs from its descendants (CDIAL 14048).
